excerpt: Niantic, maker of Pokémon GO, sold its games business to Scopely for $3.5 billion in 2025 and spun off Niantic Spatial. Its games now run as Scopely Explore.
content:
Niantic made location-based augmented reality games that send players outside to explore the real world, including Ingress, Pokémon GO, Pikmin Bloom and Monster Hunter Now, plus the community app Campfire and Wayfarer, a tool for suggesting new map locations. It began as Niantic Labs, a project inside Google led by John Hanke, and was spun out as an independent company in 2015, TechCrunch reported. Pokémon GO became a global hit after its 2016 launch, and in November 2021 Niantic raised $300 million at a $9 billion valuation to build what it called a real-world metaverse.

In March 2025 the mobile game company Scopely agreed to buy Niantic's games division for $3.5 billion; Niantic said it would add $350 million in cash for a total value of $3.85 billion to its shareholders, TechCrunch reported. Pokémon GO had more than 20 million weekly active players at the time. All employees working on the games moved to Scopely, and Niantic's mapping and AR technology business became a separate company, Niantic Spatial, led by Hanke, with $250 million in cash ($200 million from Niantic and $50 million from Scopely). Niantic's old games website now redirects to Scopely Explore, which describes itself as formerly known as Niantic.

The games remain free to play with optional in-game purchases, now run by Scopely. Anyone interested in Niantic's 3D mapping and spatial computing technology should look at Niantic Spatial instead.

We have not used Niantic for this page. It brings together Niantic's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
